methodological_rigor.justification: Rigorous biochemistry/chemical biology study with multiple orthogonal validations: amber codon suppression incorporation of AcK, TFAcK and KeK into Ub and p53; in vitro HDM2 autoubiquitination; 1H-15N HSQC NMR with chemical-shift perturbation mapping; label-free quantitative AE-MS (ANOVA S0=2, FDR=0.005) across 7 Ub variants; PRM mass spectrometry of p53 modification status; luciferase reporter assays with beta-galactosidase normalization; and confirmation by orthogonal pulldowns with recombinant UCHL3 and NDP52. Three independent replicates used throughout; proper controls (Ub 11K, 11A, 11R, 11Q). Limitations are modest: model system restricted to two proteins (Ub, p53) and two p53 residues (K120, K164), and some functional readouts (transactivation) rely on reporter constructs.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Basic science chemical-biology study; Oxford LoE 5. The p53 component provides oncology relevance by showing that acetylation status of K120/K164 modulates transcription of p21, but clinical or translational impact is indirect (improved tools for interpreting acetyllysine biology). Useful as a mechanistic lens rather than a therapeutic advance.

reporting_quality.justification: Not a clinical, observational, or preclinical animal study; no single rubric standard (CONSORT, STROBE, ARRIVE, etc.) applies so 'other' is appropriate. Methods are highly detailed: NMR instrumentation, MS acquisition, MaxQuant/Perseus pipeline versions, antibody catalog numbers, plasmid sources, and ANOVA parameters are specified. Source Data files are referenced for each figure, supporting reproducibility. Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary is referenced.

novelty_literature.justification: Builds on prior amber-codon-suppression work (including the authors' own Ub studies and Neumann/Elsasser tRNA/synthetase systems). Novel contribution is the direct comparison of AcK, TFAcK, and KeK across structural (NMR CSPs), biochemical (HDM2 autoubiquitination), interactomic (AE-MS), and functional (p53 transactivation) axes in cells, demonstrating that KeK uniquely resists cellular deacetylation while preserving acetylation-like structural/functional effects. This offers a tangible methodological tool for the acetylation field beyond incremental confirmation.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear motivation, logical progression from Ub in vitro to p53 in cells, with appropriate control comparisons (K, A, R, Q). Figures are well-structured with explicit statistical annotations. Methods are exhaustive and may be dense for non-specialist readers but are appropriate for a rigorous biochemistry paper. Minor typos (e.g., 'Ub 11AcK und Ub 11KeK') are present.

key_strengths: Orthogonal multi-method validation (NMR CSPs, HDM2 autoubiquitination, AE-MS interactomes, PRM, luciferase reporters)
Direct head-to-head comparison of AcK, TFAcK, KeK with appropriate control variants (K, A, R, Q)
Demonstrates that KeK escapes cellular deacetylation in p53, correlating with altered transactivation
Rigorous statistical thresholds (ANOVA S0=2, FDR=0.005) and triplicate biological replicates throughout
key_concerns: Translational/clinical relevance is indirect; the study is a tool-development paper rather than therapeutic advance
Generalizability tested only on Ub and two p53 residues (K120, K164); other proteins and sites may behave differently
KeK requires exogenous supplementation at millimolar concentrations and AcK-RS/tRNA machinery, limiting ease of adoption
chief_reviewer.rationale: High-quality chemical-biology methods paper with rigorous multi-modal validation and a clear tool-advance for acetylation studies; oncology relevance via p53 is real but indirect, placing the ceiling at tier 2 with minor revisions.
